prompt: Complete a static paint method that fills a white background, rotates the graphics 45 degrees around the image center, and then fills a centered red square -- which therefore appears as a diamond. Follow the steps in the starter Javadoc exactly.
explanation: Graphics2D transforms change the coordinate system for everything drawn afterwards: rotate(theta, cx, cy) spins subsequent drawing around the point (cx, cy). The background is filled before the rotation, so it stays axis-aligned; the square is filled after, so its corners swing 45 degrees outward and it renders as a diamond. That is why the tests find red at points near the center along the axes, but white at the corners of the square's original, unrotated footprint.
hints: Order matters: fill the white background BEFORE calling rotate, and draw the square AFTER.
g.rotate(Math.PI / 4, size / 2.0, size / 2.0) rotates around the image center -- the three-argument overload avoids translating by hand.
The centered square's top-left corner is at ((size - side) / 2, (size - side) / 2) with side = size / 4.
